draft_key_information_units.information: The Novaturas Group reported consolidated revenue of EUR 168 million for 2025, a 16.1% decrease from 2024, while achieving positive EBITDA of EUR 420 thousand (adjusted EBITDA) compared to negative EUR 449 thousand in 2024; the annual net loss decreased by 39% to EUR 1.17 million excluding a one-off EUR 5.7 million goodwill impairment in 2024.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword (page 4): 'served 191 thousand travellers... generated EUR 168 million in revenue... decreased by 20 percent... revenue declined by 16.1 percent... Adjusted EBITDA in 2025 amounted to EUR 420 thousand, compared with negative EUR 449 thousand in 2024... annual net loss decreased by 39 percent to EUR 1.17 million'; Main ratios table (page 6) shows 12M 2025 sales EUR 168,483k, adjusted EBITDA EUR 420k, net loss EUR (1,169)k vs 2024.

draft_key_information_units.information: Operational efficiency improved significantly in 2025, with aircraft load factor rising to 97.2% (up 1.5 pp) driven by stronger performance in Estonia (+2 pp), long-haul destinations (98.5% vs 97.4%), and ski destinations (97.2% vs 90.5%).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword (page 4): 'aircraft load factor increased by 1.5 percentage points in 2025 to 97.2 percent... strongest growth in Estonian market... load factors on long-haul destinations increased from 97.4 percent to 98.5 percent... ski destinations load factor rose from 90.5 percent to 97.2 percent.'

draft_key_information_units.information: Segment performance diverged: flight package tours saw sales fall 15.0% to EUR 145.1 million but gross profit margin improved to 15% (vs 13% in 2024); sightseeing tours by plane suffered a 23.3% sales drop and gross profit margin collapsed to 9% (vs 33% in 2024).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Segment information tables (pages 7-8): 12M 2025 flight package tours sales EUR 145,120k (-15.0% vs 2024) with gross profit margin 15% (vs 13%); sightseeing tours by plane sales EUR 2,178k (-23.3%) with gross profit margin 9% (vs 33% in 2024).

draft_key_information_units.information: The company intentionally reduced volumes on loss-making routes and prioritized higher-margin destinations, leveraging its broad portfolio to improve margins and operational efficiency despite overall revenue decline.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword (page 4): 'We intentionally reduced volumes and optimised our travel programme... reduced volumes on loss-making routes and placed greater emphasis on higher-margin destinations... improve margins and operational efficiency.' Improved Efficiency section details this strategy.

draft_key_information_units.information: 2025 results were constrained by intense competition, excess market supply in autumn affecting prices, and disruptions at Vilnius Airport from illegal cross-border activity involving unmanned balloons that reduced last-minute travel demand.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword (page 4): 'operated in an environment of intense competition and excess travel supply... increase in market-wide supply during the autumn season put pressure on prices... disruptions at Vilnius Airport related to illegal cross-border activity involving unmanned balloons reduced last-minute travel demand.'

draft_key_information_units.information: For 2026, the company plans a similar or slightly higher travel programme level, focusing on operational/cost efficiency and expanding hotel portfolio; early bookings for 2026 summer season were 59% higher year-on-year, with new destinations including Morocco and Mallorca.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword (page 4): 'For 2026, we currently plan our travel programme at a similar or slightly higher level... focus on operational and cost efficiency... expand our hotel portfolio... bookings for the 2026 summer season were 59 percent higher... new destinations: Morocco and Mallorca.'

draft_key_information_units.information: Liquidity improved with cash and cash equivalents rising to EUR 1.69 million (from EUR 0.39 million in 2024), but leverage increased significantly as debt/equity ratio climbed to 191.42% (from 121.16% in 2024); the group held EUR 21 million in travel guarantees secured by insurance/bank guarantees and EUR 4.5 million cash deposits against these.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Consolidated statements of financial position (page 18): cash and cash equivalents EUR 1,691k (2025) vs EUR 394k (2024); debt/equity ratio 191.42% (2025) vs 121.16% (2024). Notes to financial statements (page 25): 'travel guarantees amounting to EUR 21 million... cash deposits... EUR 4.5 million.'

evaluation.selection_rationale: Units were selected to cover material summary-level content per prioritization criteria: D1 provides headline financial performance (revenue, profitability, loss trends); D2 and D3 address major operational efficiency gains and segment-specific performance drivers; D4 and D5 explain key performance drivers and material market challenges; D6 covers important strategic developments for the outlook; D7 addresses material liquidity and capital position. Units are mutually independent (e.g., segment performance can be assessed without liquidity details) and exclude routine boilerplate (governance, accounting policies). All facts are source-supported without external knowledge. REFERENCE SUMMARY informed inclusion of revenue/EBITDA trends (D1), strategy (D4), and market challenges (D5), but other units derive solely from SOURCE details not condensed in the reference.
